dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:1901.text: Old. Formed from 又 and 灾. The explanation is incomplete.

shuowen:1902.text: To harmonize. Formed from 言, 又 and 炎. The large-seal form 𤎬 contains 𢆉; 𢆉 is pronounced 飪. Pronounced like 溼.

shuowen:1903.text: To draw out. Formed from 又, with 冒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1904.text: To draw out. Formed from 又, with 𢑚 indicating the sound. 𢑚 is the ancient form of 申.

shuowen:1905.text: To divide and decide. Formed from 又; the curved stroke depicts separation. [The source writes 纡 in describing that stroke.]

shuowen:1906.text: To govern. Formed from 又 and 丿: one who grasps affairs.

shuowen:1907.text: A lowered hand. Formed from 又, with 虘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1908.text: To draw out. Formed from 又, with 𠩺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1909.text: To wipe. Formed from 又 holding 巾 beneath 尸.

shuowen:1910.text: To reach. Formed from 又 and 人.

shuowen:1911.text: A bundle of grain. Formed from 又 holding 禾.

shuowen:1912.text: To turn over. Formed from 又, with 厂 in a reversed form.

shuowen:1913.text: To govern. Formed from 又 and 卪; 卪 is the regulation of affairs.

shuowen:1914.text: Smooth or slippery. The Odes says: “𠬢 and 達.” Formed from 又 and 屮. Another explanation: to take.

shuowen:1915.text: People of Chu call divining about good and ill fortune 𠭥. Formed from 又 holding 祟; 祟 also indicates the sound. Pronounced like 贅.

shuowen:1916.text: To gather. Formed from 又, with 尗 indicating the sound. In Runan, harvesting 芌 is called 叔.

shuowen:1917.text: To enter water and take something. Formed from 又 beneath 囘. 囘 is the ancient form of 回; 回 means deep water. Pronounced like 沫.

shuowen:1918.text: To capture and take. Formed from 又 and 耳. The Rites of Zhou says: “The captor takes the left ear.” The Methods of the Sima says: “Carry and present the 聝.” 聝 means an ear.

shuowen:1919.text: Bamboo for sweeping. Formed from 又 holding 甡.

shuowen:1920.text: To borrow. The explanation is missing.

shuowen:1921.text: Those sharing the same intention are friends. Formed from two 又, expressing friendship with one another. [The source writes 𢖽 in the opening phrase.]

shuowen:1922.text: Laws and standards. Formed from 又, with abbreviated 庶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1923.text: The left hand. A pictograph. All characters in the 𠂇 category are formed from 𠂇.

shuowen:1924.text: Lowly; one who performs service. Formed from 𠂇 and 甲.

shuowen:1925.text: One who records affairs. Formed from 又 holding 中; 中 means uprightness. All characters in the 史 category are formed from 史.

shuowen:1926.text: An office or duty. Formed from 史, with abbreviated 之 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1927.text: To remove a bamboo branch. Formed from a hand holding half a bamboo. All characters in the 支 category are formed from 支.

shuowen:1928.text: To hold and carry away. Formed from 支, with 奇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1929.text: The hand's swift skill. Formed from 又 holding 巾. All characters in the 𦘒 category are formed from 𦘒.

shuowen:1930.text: To practice or become accustomed. Formed from 𦘒, with 㣇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1931.text: To handle affairs with vigilant respect. Formed from 𦘒 above 𣶒, expressing trembling caution.

shuowen:1932.text: That with which one writes. Chu calls it 聿, Wu 不律, and Yan 弗. Formed from 𦘒, with 一 indicating the sound. All characters in the 聿 category are formed from 聿.

shuowen:1933.text: In Qin it is called 筆, a writing brush. Formed from 聿 and 竹.

shuowen:1934.text: Ornamentation with a brush. Formed from 聿 and 彡. Common speech calls fine writing 𦘔. Pronounced like 𣸁.

shuowen:1935.text: To set down in writing. Formed from 聿, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1936.text: A boundary. It depicts the four boundaries of a field; 聿 is that with which one draws them. All characters in the 畫 category are formed from 畫.

shuowen:1937.text: The sun's coming out and going in, forming the boundary with night. Formed from abbreviated 畫 and 日.

shuowen:1938.text: To reach. Formed from 又 and abbreviated 㞑. 又 holding the tail means catching up from behind. All characters in the 隶 category are formed from 隶.

shuowen:1939.text: To reach. Formed from 隶, with 枲 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Before Heaven has brought clouds and rain.”

shuowen:1940.text: To be attached. Formed from 隶, with 柰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1941.text: Firm. Formed from 又, with 臣 indicating the sound. All characters in the 臤 category are formed from 臤. Pronounced like 鏗 in 鏗鏘. Ancient writing uses it for 賢.

shuowen:1942.text: Silk tightly wound. Formed from 臤 and abbreviated 絲.

shuowen:1943.text: Hard. Formed from 臤 and 土.

shuowen:1944.text: To stand upright. Formed from 臤, with 豆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1945.text: To be led or drawn; to serve a lord. It depicts bending in submission. All characters in the 臣 category are formed from 臣.

shuowen:1946.text: To diverge. Formed from two 臣 facing away from one another. Pronounced like 誑.

shuowen:1947.text: Good. Formed from 臣, with 戕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1948.text: An implement used to strike people apart. The Rites says: “The 殳 is of layered bamboo, eight-sided, one zhang and two feet long, mounted on a war chariot; the chariot guards go ahead as vanguard.” Formed from 又, with 几 indicating the sound. All characters in the 殳 category are formed from 殳.

shuowen:1949.text: A 殳 staff. Formed from 殳, with 示 indicating the sound. Another account: at city walls, markets and lanes a sheepskin is hung high; when someone not entitled to enter tries to do so, it is briefly lowered to frighten cattle and horses, called 祋. Hence formed from 示 and 殳. The Odes says: “Carrying dagger-axes and 祋.”

shuowen:1950.text: The 殳 staff carried by soldiers in an army. Formed from 木 and 殳. The Methods of the Sima says: “Hold feathers and follow with staffs.”

shuowen:1951.text: To strike and hit one another, as carriages collide; hence formed from 殳 and 軎.

shuowen:1952.text: To strike downward from above. Another explanation: plain or white. Formed from 殳, with 𡉉 indicating the sound. 𡉉 has the fanqie 苦江.

shuowen:1953.text: To strike upward from below. Formed from 殳, with 冘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1954.text: To strike with a swinging motion. Formed from 殳, with 豆 indicating the sound. The ancient form of 祋 is like this.

shuowen:1955.text: To strike a suspended object. Formed from 殳, with 𠃬 indicating the sound. [The action described by 𣪐 is uncertain.]

shuowen:1956.text: To strike an object with a mallet. Formed from 殳, with 豖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1957.text: To beat an object. Formed from 殳, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1958.text: To strike the head. Formed from 殳, with 高 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1959.text: The sound of striking. Formed from 殳, with 𡱂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1960.text: The sound of a strike hitting its mark. Formed from 殳, with 医 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1961.text: To pound an object. Formed from 殳, with abbreviated 耑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1962.text: The sound of striking something hollow. Formed from 殳, with 宮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1963.text: To mingle and mix. Formed from 殳, with 肴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1964.text: Rash anger. Another explanation: decisiveness. Formed from 殳, with 豙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1965.text: To bend by working or rubbing. Formed from 殳 and 𠧢; 𠧢 is the ancient form of 叀. The character 廏 contains this element.

shuowen:1966.text: To serve on the frontier. Formed from 殳 and 彳.

shuowen:1967.text: 㱾改: a large 剛卯 amulet for driving away spirits and ghosts. Formed from 殳, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1968.text: To kill. Formed from 殳, with 杀 indicating the sound. All characters in the 殺 category are formed from 殺.

shuowen:1969.text: A minister killing his lord. The Changes says: “A minister murders his lord.” Formed from abbreviated 殺, with 式 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1970.text: A short-feathered bird flying in the manner 𠘧𠘧. A pictograph. All characters in the 𠘧 category are formed from 𠘧. Pronounced like 殊. [The precise flight description is uncertain.]

shuowen:1971.text: To fly with newly grown feathers. Formed from 𠘧 and 彡.

shuowen:1972.text: The 舒鳧, namely a duck, 鶩. Formed from 鳥, with 𠘧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1973.text: Ten divisions. One inch back from the hand, the moving pulse is called the 寸口. Formed from 又 and 一. All characters in the 寸 category are formed from 寸.

shuowen:1974.text: A court, where laws and standards are maintained. Formed from 寸, with 之 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1975.text: To lead or command. Formed from 寸, with abbreviated 𤖕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1976.text: To unravel and order. Formed from 工, 口, 又 and 寸. 工 and 口 are disorder; 又 and 寸 divide and arrange it. 彡 indicates the sound. This shares the idea of 𤕦. As a measure, the span of a person's two arms is a 尋, eight feet.

shuowen:1977.text: A six-inch tablet. Formed from 寸, with 叀 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 專 is a spindle whorl.

shuowen:1978.text: To spread. Formed from 寸, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1979.text: 導 means to lead. Formed from 寸, with 道 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1980.text: What is stripped off an animal as hide is called 皮. Formed from 又, with abbreviated 爲 indicating the sound. All characters in the 皮 category are formed from 皮.

shuowen:1981.text: A swelling arising on the face. Formed from 皮, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1982.text: A dark complexion of the face. Formed from 皮, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1983.text: Cracks in the feet. Formed from 皮, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1984.text: Fine raised wrinkles of skin. Formed from 皮, with 夋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1985.text: To soften leather. Formed from 北, abbreviated 皮 and abbreviated 敻. All characters in the 㼱 category are formed from 㼱. Pronounced like 耎; another pronunciation is like 雋.

shuowen:1986.text: Leather trousers for hunting with feathered banners. Formed from 㼱, with 灷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1987.text: To strike lightly. Formed from 又, with 卜 indicating the sound. All characters in the 攴 category are formed from 攴.

shuowen:1988.text: To teach. Formed from 攴, with 启 indicating the sound. The Analects says: “Unless eager to understand, he is not enlightened.”

shuowen:1989.text: To pass through. Formed from 彳, 攴 and 育.

shuowen:1990.text: To strike. Formed from 攴, with abbreviated 肈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1991.text: Swift. Formed from 攴, with 每 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1992.text: Strong. Formed from 攴, with 民 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1993.text: Strong. Formed from 攴, with 矛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1994.text: To press or constrain. Formed from 攴, with 白 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “The regular 敀 and the regular appointees.” [The quoted office term is uncertain.]

shuowen:1995.text: To put in order. Formed from 攴, 束 and 正; 正 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1996.text: To imitate. Formed from 攴, with 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1997.text: To cause something to be done. Formed from 攴, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1998.text: To correct. Formed from 攴 and 正; 正 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1999.text: To spread or bestow, 𢾭. Formed from 攴, with 也 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 施.

shuowen:2000.text: To spread or bestow, 𢻱. Formed from 攴, with 尃 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Thereby transmit it to later generations.”
